subject: ACME integration — post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-14T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: ACME integration — post-call recap & next steps

Alex — thanks again for the demo and for walking through the use cases. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Pain points you mentioned:
- Inconsistent summary quality from your current on-prem LLMs, especially for long conversation histories (lossy truncation).
- Cost unpredictability during high-throughput periods for chat and reranking flows.
- Need for streaming and function-calling to show real-time status updates back to your ticketing system.
- Desire for structured outputs (JSON) from summaries so downstream systems can parse entities and action items.

Goals we captured:
- Improve summary fidelity for 10k+ token histories with lower latency.
- Add a streaming layer so your UI shows incremental results and can call back for actions (function calling).
- Use embeddings + reranking to surface the most relevant docs (KB) at query time.
- Pilot with 2 internal teams, then expand if latency/cost targets met.

Product fit / integration notes we discussed:
- SDK changes: we recommend the hosted SDK (Python/TS) for initial integration; we can provide sample snippets that show streaming + function-calling combined with structured JSON outputs.
- Streaming: Redwood streaming will let you render partial outputs in the UI; it supports early token heuristics to show high-confidence fields first.
- Function calling: Redwood’s function-calling layer maps model outputs to typed function signatures; we can demonstrate mapping that to your /tickets/update API.
- Embeddings + reranking: we’ll propose an embeddings pipeline with per-index quantization options to balance recall and cost.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with your engineering team (Nikhil suggested Wed/Thu this week) — runthrough of sample prompts, streaming demo, and function-calling mapping.
2) Provide a short integration proposal + sample SDK snippets (I’ll attach a proposal and a zip with code examples).
3) Create a short trial account with rate limits aligned to your pilot.
4) Procurement intro from your side when you’re ready — we’ll prepare an initial SOW and pricing benchmark.

Requested owners / timelines:
- Redwood: Marissa to deliver proposal + SDK snippets by EOD Tue (2026-06-15).
- Redwood: Nikhil to run technical deep-dive and share a sample function schema during the call.
- ACME: Alex to confirm attendees and preferred time for the deep-dive.

Attachment: redwood-integration-proposal.pdf, sample-sdk-snippets.zip

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful and captures everything we talked about. A few quick clarifications:
- For streaming, our UI team wants to see examples where structured fields (like priority/entity) come back before the full prose so we can render status badges.
- On the embeddings/reranking side, we have a 50M doc KB but can start with the 100k subset for the pilot.
- Procurement will likely want an initial 3-month committed capacity for the pilot. I’ll loop them in on timing.

We’re available for a deep-dive Thu 2026-06-17 10:00am PT — that works for the engineering team. Please lock that if it works for you and Nikhil.

—Alex
